items.title: A tight Gaussian law is carried by a separable closed subspace
items.statement: A tight centered Borel Gaussian probability on any real Banach space is carried by a separable closed linear subspace E; as an E-valued law it remains tight and Gaussian, and its ambient support equals its support in E.
items.strategy: Choose compact sets with probabilities tending to one, take the closed rational span of their countable dense union, and use Hahn–Banach to extend continuous linear functionals from E to the ambient Banach space.

items.title: The L² link norm controls binary-regression likelihood distances
items.statement: For q_w(x,y)=Ψ(w(x))^y(1−Ψ(w(x)))^{1−y} relative to G⊗counting measure, with G a probability and L=sup|Ψ′|, R=sup|Ψ′/[Ψ(1−Ψ)]| finite, d₂(q_w,q_{w0})²≤2L²‖w−w0‖²_{L²(G)}, KL(Q_0∥Q_w)≤LR‖w−w0‖²_{L²(G)}/2, and E_0[log(q_w/q_{w0})²]≤R²‖w−w0‖²_{L²(G)}.
items.strategy: Use the mean-value bound for Ψ, differentiate the Bernoulli directional KL in its second logit, and bound both Bernoulli log-probability derivatives by R.

items.title: Empirical mean and scale distance control Gaussian-regression likelihoods
items.statement: For independent Y_i∼N(w_0(x_i),σ_0²), model Y_i∼N(w(x_i),σ²), σ,σ0∈[a,b] with 0<a<b, and max_i|w(x_i)−w0(x_i)|≤1, |σ−σ0|≤1, the averages of KL(P_{i0}∥P_i) and E_0[log(p_i/p_{i0})²] are each bounded by C_{a,b}(‖w−w0‖_n²+|σ−σ0|²).
items.strategy: Compute the normal KL formula and expand the log likelihood ratio as a constant plus linear and centered quadratic functions of the true Gaussian error; bound the scale-only term by its vanishing first derivative at σ0.

items.title: Linear and quadratic Gaussian statistics have exponential tails
items.statement: For an integer n>=1, independent standard normals Z_i, fixed c_i, σ≤b, and Q=n^{-1}∑(δ_i+σZ_i)² with ‖δ‖_n≤1, the centered linear statistic n^{-1}∑c_iσZ_i has two-sided tail 2exp(−nt²/(2σ²‖c‖_n²)); for 0<t≤b²+2, P(|Q−(σ²+‖δ‖_n²)|≥t)≤2exp(−nt²/(4V_b)), V_b=2b⁴+4b².
items.strategy: Complete the square to compute the scalar Gaussian moment generating function and the noncentral squared-normal moment generating function; bound the latter near zero and optimize the exponential-Markov inequality.

items.title: Local KL and log-square mass bounds a non-IID posterior denominator
items.statement: For independent dominated observations and a prior subset of mass at least e^{−Cnε²} on which average directional KL and average log-likelihood second moment are each at most ε², the full likelihood-ratio denominator is finite almost surely and is at least e^{−(C+2)nε²} with probability at least 1−1/(nε²).
items.strategy: Bound the integrated likelihood ratio in expectation using independence and Tonelli; Jensen lower-bounds the denominator by the prior-averaged log likelihood, whose mean and variance are bounded by nε², and Chebyshev gives the stated event.

items.title: Tests and a sieve tail imply posterior contraction from a denominator bound
items.statement: If a dominated full-data likelihood denominator is at least e^{−A nε²} with probability tending to one, the prior mass outside a measurable sieve is at most e^{−B nε²} with B>A, and a test has null and uniform sieve type-II errors at most e^{−T nε²} with T>A, then posterior mass outside the tested set tends to zero in P0 probability.
items.strategy: Split the likelihood numerator into tested sieve mass and sieve tail, change measure to bound their expectations, and apply Markov after dividing by the denominator lower bound.

items.title: A nonzero Gaussian direction forces logarithmic small-ball cost
items.statement:
Let $W$ be a centered Gaussian random element in a real normed space $B$. Let $\ell\in B^*$ satisfy $\operatorname{Var}(\ell(W))=\tau^2>0$, and let $\mathbb H$ be a Hilbert subspace of $B$ with nonnegative squared norm. For $w_0\in B$, define
$$\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon)=\inf_{\substack{h\in\mathbb H\\\|h-w_0\|_B<\epsilon}}\left\{\|h\|_{\mathbb H}^2\right\}-\log\Pr(\|W\|_B<\epsilon),$$
with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$. Then for every $\epsilon>0$,
$$\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon)\ge \log(1/\epsilon)-C_\ell,\qquad C_\ell=\log\!\left(\frac{2\|\ell\|_{B^*}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\tau}\right).$$

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, equation (1.2)
Bas J. K. Kleijn, Aad W. van der Vaart and Harry van Zanten, Lectures on Nonparametric Bayesian Statistics, Definition 11.7 and Theorem 12.1

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the standard-normal probability law.

items.title: Supremum distance controls local log-Gaussian density distances
items.statement: For p_w=e^w/∫e^w dν and p_0=p_{w_0}, if both normalizers are finite and positive and r=‖w−w_0‖∞≤1, then h(p_w,p_0)≤e^r r, KL(P_0∥P_w)≤(e^{2r}/2)r², and E_0[log(p_w/p_0)²]≤4r².
items.strategy: Write g=w−w0 and c=log E0 e^g. Bound |c|≤r, apply the exponential Taylor remainder to the centered g for directional KL, and bound the normalized log-density ratio pointwise for Hellinger and its second moment.

items.title: Supremum sieves admit tests in fixed-design Gaussian regression
items.statement: For fixed design, σ∈[a,b], ε_n→0, nε_n²→∞ and a measurable sieve B_n with log N(3ε_n,B_n,‖·‖∞)≤6C nε_n², for any T>0 a sufficiently large fixed M gives tests of H0:(w0,σ0) against (w,σ)∈B_n×[a,b] with ‖w−w0‖_n+|σ−σ0|>Mε_n whose null and uniform alternative errors are at most e^{−Tnε_n²}.
items.strategy: Cover the mean functions; use Gaussian linear-score tests when the empirical mean distance is large and upper/lower residual-energy tests when the scale distance is large; union-bound the finite cover and use the Gaussian quadratic tail bound.

items.title: Gaussian-process posterior contraction in density and regression models
items.statement:
Let $\epsilon_n>0$ satisfy $\epsilon_n\to0$ and $n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$. For the centered tight Gaussian prior in each branch, let $\mu$ be its law and let $B$ be a separable closed Banach carrier with the norm inherited from that branch's stated function space, as supplied by [[lem-tight-borel-gaussian-law-has-separable-support]]. Write $\mathbb H$ for the covariance RKHS of $\mu$ on $B$, and define
$$\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon)=\inf_{\substack{h\in\mathbb H\\\|h-w_0\|_B<\epsilon}}\left\{\|h\|_{\mathbb H}^2-\log\mu(\epsilon B^\circ)\right\},\qquad \epsilon B^\circ=\{u\in B:\|u\|_B<\epsilon\}.$$
Suppose $\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon_n)\le n\epsilon_n^2$.

In each branch, parameter-to-data densities are jointly measurable and the posterior $\Pi_n$ is the data-indexed normalization of the prior times the likelihood on fibers with finite positive evidence.

1. **Log-Gaussian density estimation.** On a measurable space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A)$ with sigma-finite measure $\nu$, let $W$ be a tight centered Borel Gaussian random element in $\ell^\infty(\mathsf X)$, and let $w_0$ belong to its support. Assume path evaluation $(w,x)\mapsto w(x)$ is jointly measurable, $Z_w=\int e^w\,d\nu\in(0,\infty)$ for prior-almost every $w$ and for $w_0$, and set $p_w=e^w/Z_w$, $p_0=p_{w_0}$. For IID data $X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim P_0$, sufficiently large fixed $M$ gives
$$E_0\Pi_n\{w:h(P_w,P_0)>M\epsilon_n\mid X^n\}\longrightarrow0.$$
When $0<\nu(\mathsf X)<\infty$, bounded paths imply the required normalizers are finite and positive.

2. **Binary regression.** Let $(X_i,Y_i)$ be IID, with $X_i\sim G$, $Y_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $P_0(Y=1\mid X=x)=f_0(x)=\Psi(w_0(x))\in(0,1)$. Assume $\Psi:\mathbb R\to(0,1)$ is differentiable, $\sup|\Psi'|<\infty$, and $\sup|\Psi'/[\Psi(1-\Psi)]|<\infty$. Suppose the prior is either a tight centered Gaussian law in $L^2(G)$ with a jointly measurable evaluation version representing its $L^2(G)$ element almost everywhere, or a tight centered Gaussian law in $\ell^\infty(\mathsf X)$ with jointly measurable evaluation and bounded $w_0$; in either case $w_0$ belongs to the prior support. Then for sufficiently large fixed $M$,
$$E_0\Pi_n\{\|\Psi(w)-f_0\|_{L^2(G)}>M\epsilon_n\mid (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\}\longrightarrow0.$$

3. **Fixed-design Gaussian regression.** For deterministic $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, assume independent $Y_i\sim N(w_0(x_i),\sigma_0^2)$, a centered tight Borel Gaussian prior $W$ in $\ell^\infty(\mathsf X)$ with $w_0$ in support, and an independent prior on the standard deviation $\sigma$ supported on a fixed $[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$ containing $\sigma_0$, with Lebesgue density bounded below by a positive constant. Put $\rho_n=\max\{\epsilon_n,\sqrt{\log n/n}\}$ for $n\ge2$. Then for sufficiently large fixed $M$,
$$E_0\Pi_n\{\|w-w_0\|_n+|\sigma-\sigma_0|>M\rho_n\mid Y_{1:n}\}\longrightarrow0.$$
The sharper conclusion with $\epsilon_n$ in place of $\rho_n$ holds if the Gaussian law is not the point mass at zero. It also holds when $W=0$ almost surely and the scale-prior density is bounded above on a neighborhood of $\sigma_0$; this extra upper bound is needed only for that sharper degenerate-prior alternative, not for the universal $\rho_n$ conclusion. In the nondegenerate case $\rho_n=O(\epsilon_n)$, so the two formulations differ only by the fixed constant $M$. Here $\|w-w_0\|_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_i(w(x_i)-w_0(x_i))^2$.

The concentration-function hypothesis is interpreted on a separable Banach space carrying the prior. For a tight Gaussian law initially given in nonseparable $\ell^\infty(\mathsf X)$, the separable-support reduction is [[lem-tight-borel-gaussian-law-has-separable-support]]; the norm and prior law are restricted to that support space.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, §§2–3
Bas J. K. Kleijn, Aad W. van der Vaart and Harry van Zanten, Lectures on Nonparametric Bayesian Statistics, Chapters 9 and 12
Subhashis Ghosal and Aad W. van der Vaart, Convergence rates of posterior distributions for noniid observations, §§2–3

items.axiom_use: AC and countable choice are inherited from the Gaussian support/concentration chain; AC is also used by the directional-KL and normal-law suppliers. The separate relative Hahn–Banach principle is an explicit premise for the separable-support reduction and is not silently inferred from AC.

items.title: A degenerate GP concentration function does not bound unknown-scale prior mass
items.statement:
Let $W\equiv0$, $w_0=0$, and let its covariance RKHS be $\mathbb H=\{0\}$. Define $\phi_0(\epsilon)=\inf_{h\in\mathbb H,\,|h-w_0|<\epsilon}\{\|h\|_{\mathbb H}^2\}-\log\Pr(|W|<\epsilon)$. For $n$ large, set $\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log\log n/n}$ and take an independent $\sigma\sim\operatorname{Unif}[1/2,3/2]$ with true value $\sigma_0=1$. Then $\phi_0(\epsilon_n)=0$, $\epsilon_n\to0$, and $n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$, but
$$-\log\Pr(|\sigma-\sigma_0|<\epsilon_n)\not=O(n\epsilon_n^2).$$
Thus the Gaussian concentration condition alone does not verify the joint local prior-mass bound used by the denominator argument for the unknown-scale branch. This calculation is a proof-gap example, not a posterior counterexample.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, §3.3
Subhashis Ghosal and Aad W. van der Vaart, Convergence rates of posterior distributions for noniid observations, §3

items.title: Small L² log-density perturbations can remain far in Hellinger distance
items.statement: For integers k>=1, on [0,1] with Lebesgue measure, w_k=k 1_[0,k^{-4}] tends to zero in L² while the normalized log-density p_k=e^{w_k}/∫e^{w_k} remains at Hellinger distance tending to √2 from the uniform truth.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the L² norm, normalizer and Hellinger affinity explicitly; the normalized prior density concentrates on the shrinking spike.

items.title: A spiky scale prior defeats an arbitrary degenerate-Gaussian concentration rate

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, Section 3.3

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the normal-law interface. The prior and subsequences are explicitly specified; no new choice beyond these declared probability interfaces is used.
items.statement: For every centered tight Gaussian prior, including $W=0$, a Gaussian concentration condition $\phi_0(\epsilon_n)\le n\epsilon_n^2$, $\epsilon_n\to0$ and $n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$, together with an independent scale prior on a fixed positive compact interval having density bounded below, would imply expected posterior contraction at a sufficiently large fixed multiple of $\epsilon_n$ in fixed-design Gaussian regression. The following counterexample concerns that unrestricted rate claim, not the universal logarithmic-floor or sharper qualified alternatives proved on the A page.

items.title: A constant Gaussian log-density prior gives the uniform density exactly
items.statement: On $[0,1]$ with Lebesgue measure, take $W(x)=Z$ for all $x$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$, and let the truth be $w_0=0$. The normalized log-Gaussian density prior is exactly the point mass at the uniform density. The concentration condition holds at $\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}$ for all sufficiently large n.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, §3.1
Bas J. K. Kleijn, Aad W. van der Vaart and Harry van Zanten, Lectures on Nonparametric Bayesian Statistics, §12.2

items.title: A one-point logistic GP regression satisfies the L² link branch
items.statement: Let the covariate space contain one point $x_0$, let $G=\delta_{x_0}$, and take $W(x_0)=Z\sim N(0,1)$. With the logistic link $\Psi(u)=(1+e^{-u})^{-1}$ and truth $w_0(x_0)=0$, the hypotheses of the binary-regression branch hold at $\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}$ for all sufficiently large n.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, §3.2, Theorem 3.2
Bas J. K. Kleijn, Aad W. van der Vaart and Harry van Zanten, Lectures on Nonparametric Bayesian Statistics, Chapters 9–10

items.title: A constant GP on a repeated fixed design meets the nondegenerate scale branch
items.statement: Take repeated design point $x_0$, prior $W(x)=Z\sim N(0,1)$, truth $w_0=0$, true standard deviation $\sigma_0=1$, and an independent prior $\sigma\sim\operatorname{Unif}[1/2,3/2]$. For $\epsilon_n=2\sqrt{\log n/n}$, the GP concentration and scale-local-mass conditions hold for all sufficiently large n.

references.title: A. W. van der Vaart and J. H. van Zanten, Rates of contraction of posterior distributions based on Gaussian process priors, §3.3, Theorem 3.3
Subhashis Ghosal and Aad W. van der Vaart, Convergence rates of posterior distributions for noniid observations, §3
